title: Regional Scope Onboarding Playbook with Contracting Hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Playbook and templated forms to triage enterprise requests for new region availability, residency constraints, and failover contracts. This artifact codifies the operational decision ladder plus the contract- and SOW-level hooks (pricing adjustments, SLAs, data handling clauses) required before engineering or infra provisioning is scheduled. It aims to reduce back-and-forth between Sales, Legal, Product, and Engineering by providing a repeatable intake questionnaire, acceptance gates, and an executable follow-up checklist.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form covers legal, technical, and commercial signals: residency requirement, encryption/KMS expectations, traffic failover window, estimated qps, and retention constraints
Triage matrix maps each request to one of: Immediate (self-serve), Scheduled (Dedicated allocation), Private onboarding (VPC/on-prem), or Declined with remediation guidance
Contracting hooks documented for each path: minimum term, committed capacity, pricing uplift tiers, SLA language snippets, required audit artifacts
Operational playbook includes an estimated timeline and owner for each stage (Legal review, Infra scoping, Capacity commit, Customer validation)
Pilot checklist and rollback/fallback policy defined for initial rollouts in a new region

decision_points: Minimum committed capacity threshold for offering Reserved region onboarding (recommended: 50k tokens/sec sustained)
When to require Private deployment (customer data residency + audit > 36 months retention or HCLS/Finance regulated workloads)
Pricing uplift schedule and discount cadence tied to 12-month vs 36-month commitments
Whether an initial trial can be provisioned in Hosted with strict IP/contractual addendum vs mandating Private deployment
Fallback policies and allowed automatic failover windows for customers with strict residency requirements
